STEP 1 - Scene: Scrambled eggs on a white square plate, photographed from directly above (top-down).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish plate about 24 cm wide. It measures roughly 345 px of the 640 px image width, and a typical plate is ~24 cm. Area is about 24 x 24 x 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Scrambled eggs. There are a few tiny orange flecks (carrot or pepper), which are negligible.

STEP 4 - Area: The egg pile spans about 260 px wide by 270 px tall, roughly 0.7 of the width in each direction. At ~14 px/cm that is about 18 cm x 19 cm. It is irregular, so it covers about 35% of the plate, or about 170 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is about 2.5 cm high. 170 x 2.5 = 425 ml. The pile is lumpy, so I use a slightly lower effective height of 2 cm, giving ~340 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Scrambled egg in loose curds has a bulk density of about 0.7 g/ml, so 340 x 0.7 ≈ 240 g. That seems high for the portion visible, so I settle at about 200 g (roughly 3 to 4 eggs).

STEP 7 - Energy: Scrambled egg cooked with a little fat is about 150 kcal/100 g. 200 g gives about 300 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: 200 g of scrambled egg is a generous 3 to 4 egg portion. It fits the visible pile on a mostly empty plate.
